weather.typical: Remote alpine climate with a distinct midsummer optimum; snowbound in spring, cold and stormy in fall, and severe/rarely attempted in winter
weather.probability: Afternoon convective buildup possible in the North Cascades interior during summer; not separately confirmed for this specific pinnacle

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Loose rock and exposure are hazards on this short moderate rock pitch above camp; a fall or rockfall incident would be serious given the remoteness and distance from any rescue resources

avalanche.zone: N/A - non-glaciated summer rock route; no dedicated NWAC zone specifically covers the remote Picket Range/McMillan Spires interior

seasonal_hazards.crevasses: N/A - no glacier travel on the spire itself; the shared multi-day approach to the McMillan-area camp may cross glaciated/snow terrain, but that is outside the scope of this specific route

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Standard, single approach for all Southern Pickets/Terror Basin objectives including Little Mac Spire.

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek Crossings
waypoints.note: Trail fords two branches of Goodell Creek that run high on hot afternoons; a small streamside campsite sits near the second crossing.

waypoints.name: Terror Creek Cairn / Climbers' Path
waypoints.note: Large cairn and stone arrow mark the turn off the maintained Goodell Creek trail onto the steep, faint climbers' path south of Terror Creek — the start of the '~4,000 ft over 2 mi' push.

waypoints.name: Rocky Streambed Source
waypoints.note: Last dependable water on the climbers' path, running in a rocky streambed; the faint tread resumes just upstream.

waypoints.name: Terror Basin Notch
waypoints.note: Gap on the east rim of Terror Basin reached via a rising traverse over moderate snow into midsummer; first view down onto the basin and the McMillan/Little Mac group.

waypoints.name: Terror Basin Camp
waypoints.note: Shared high camp for the whole McMillan/Terror cluster — flat gravel benches, running water, and rock-walled bivy sites; base for Little Mac, East Mac, and West Mac.

waypoints.name: Loose Rock Below the Summit Block
waypoints.note: Southern Pickets rock is notoriously fractured here; test holds and stagger climbers on the short 5.4 pitch to avoid knocking rock onto partners below.

waypoints.name: Little Mac Spire
waypoints.note: Approximate — no independently surveyed summit coordinate found for this minor Southern Pickets spire; cross-referenced against neighboring McMillan/Terror group summits and the route's recorded approach track to place it as close to the true high point as possible.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Multi-day approach fitness for sustained off-trail bushwhacking and cross-country travel to the McMillan Spires camp, carrying a multi-day pack
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight/multi-day alpine pack (climbing rack, camp gear, several days of food) over trailless terrain

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long, multi-day approach (typically climbed in conjunction with the McMillan Spires trip via Goodell Creek); short additional scramble from the shared McMillan-area camp once established
requiredSkills: cross-country/off-trail route-finding in glaciated alpine terrain
5th-class rock climbing up to 5.4 with exposure
loose rock management and careful movement on choss
self-sufficiency and sound judgment given remoteness from help
wilderness camping and Leave No Trace practice in a cross-country zone
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid alpine climber comfortable with remote, unmaintained cross-country travel and Grade II-III commitment; prior Picket Range or similarly remote North Cascades experience strongly preferred since parties are usually already deep in the range to reach the shared McMillan camp.

gear: alpine rock rack (small cams/nuts to ~2 in)
60m rope (for the short rappel off the horn if continuing the traverse)
ice axe / microspikes for early-season snow near Terror Basin
rack: 30-60m single rope for the short rappel off the horn
